utterances.text: No, the -- that also relates to the UNDU. There's some certain time Mr. Karadzic to be there, the dead-line, and the -- we cannot go over past ten minutes. So if you could divide into two minutes, two and a half minutes, let's do that. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have a look at 65 ter 19717.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for information, the picture is one of the associated exhibits dealt with in his amalgamated statement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's Exhibit P3961, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you give this interview to the Dutch parliamentary group -- sorry, I guess the number is not the right one. This is not the document. 65 ter 19717. In 2002 did you talk to a Dutch parliamentary group?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am going to read this to you now while we're waiting for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENDERS ASKED YOU
utterances.text: [In English] "Did you observe any violation of human rights committed in the compound by Bosnian Serbs. "Mr. Rutten: No." [Interpretation] And then further on -- I think this is it, this is the document. Can we look at the next page now. Do you remember this conversation?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further on -- well, I guess it's the next page then, the next one then. Did you say there that you had not seen -- at that location you say the president is ask you. [In English] "But you, yourself, did not see war crimes committed at that location"?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES RUTTEN
utterances.text: It's speaking about inside the compound, inside our area, inside our camp. So I think you're a little bit off line here because this is what I stated then and it's right and it has nothing to do what I earlier stated in this statement just right now here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Talking about bus depot as well, you're not only talking about the compound. You are talking about a broader area. Is that right? I simply cannot find the page but this is what you say. [In English] [As read] "The Potocari compound was a section in which the UN was housed as well as the remains of the battalion. The bus depot was to the south of this. Obviously things were going on there. We did try to prevent some of this happening, but I personally did not see any direct violation of human rights, only threats."

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES RUTTEN
utterances.text: Again, this is right because this is speaking about the bus remise or where the bus -- former bus station and not about other areas where I was during the last days of the enclave -- before the fall of the enclave. So there is nothing in conflict in between the statement right here and what I did in front of the hearing committee in the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry to interrupt. I just don't want to lose my time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to tender this page, or rather -- or rather, these paragraphs if not the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. There --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll find the page and we'll let you know which page it is. I'm done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1954. And just to correct the record, Your Honours, previously 1D4880 was assigned MFI D1951, it should, in fact, be MFI D1952. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And list of war criminals can be admitted. Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will give the number then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1957, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Colonel, on line 50 of today's transcript, the accused asked you about your Krstic testimony in which you talked about the type of ammunition -- excuse me, the type of munitions that the BH army had. He did not ask you about the ammunition that the BH army had which was in your Krstic testimony. Can you tell us how much ammunition the BH army had.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, it was very scarce what they had, at least what they told me and what we saw from them. So there wasn't much around. Now -- and the main part of what they had, at least what they said to us and what we find out, was that they had been given into our weapons collections point.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Also in today's transcript, page 90, when you were talking about the photo of the burning IDs, line 10, you said: "This happened in the day after the 13th, after most of the Serbs had left already." Did you mean Serbs or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES RUTTEN
utterances.text: Muslims had left already.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. And we're going to call up D1039 on Sanction. This is a document that Mr. Karadzic showed you. It's dated July 11th, 1995. If you look at the first page, you had indicated that at the time, whatever this said, this was not what was going on on the ground and he read to you a portion of this document. I'll just note it's July 11th and the stamp indicates that it was received at 2200 hours, so it's late in the night. Number 1: "The purpose of this message is to inform you of plans I am making to deal with the situation in Srebrenica ..." And then if we go to page 2, which is section (b) you were asked about this section as well. And I'll read it out for the record. This says: "Following consultations with the Bosnian government and in order to avoid a continuing humanitarian catastrophe, agreement will be solicited from the Bosnian Serbs to allow all residents of Srebrenica, including all men, to leave for Tuzla if they so wish." Colonel, you were on the ground as this was going on that night and the following day, is this what was happening on the ground, were all residents of Srebrenica, including all men, allowed to leave for Tuzla if they wished?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: What was happening on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES RUTTEN
utterances.text: On the ground men were separated and by portions in buses leaving from the white house out of the enclave through OP Papa.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And just page 3, the bottom of page 3 of this document, it says, "Actions from the Security Council." And this is what Akashi is requesting from the Security Council. When you go to 4(e), which is -- apologies, but this is the last page, 4(e) says: "All those wishing to leave Srebrenica for Tuzla must be allowed to do so under UNHCR care." Now, this is something Akashi was asking for. Did this ever come to fruition?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, Colonel Rutten. Thank you on behalf of the Chamber and the Tribunal for your coming again to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are free to go and have a safe journey back to your place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will resume 9.00 tomorrow. I thank all the staff for their indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of November, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.13 p.m.,
